welcome.text: Welcome to a space to pause, reflect, and reconnect with clarity and calm…

relaxWithIn.name: Sound & Breath
relaxWithIn.description: A guided sound bath experience combined with breathing techniques to help you slow down, relax and reconnect with yourself.

nadaAcupuncture.name: Relax with NADA
nadaAcupuncture.description: NADA ear acupuncture is a simple five-point treatment that supports relaxation and helps you slow down. It is often used during periods of stress, inner restlessness, and sleep difficulties, offering a moment to reconnect with a sense of calm and balance.

cacaoAndMe.name: My Story
cacaoAndMe.description: Behind SF Nature is my own journey of learning to listen to myself a little earlier, slow down when I need to, and find balance in an active life. What I share today has grown from what I have learned, experienced and tried along the way.

cacaoMindfulness.name: Cacao Mindfulness Practice
cacaoMindfulness.description: Cacao mindfulness practice combines warm cacao with reflection and presence. It offers a simple and effective way to slow down, reduce stress, and create space for clarity and balance in everyday life.

about.title: About Cacao Mindfulness Practice
about.description1: offers a structured way to pause, recharge, and sharpen focus. With the support of ceremonial cacao, practical mindfulness tools, and a calm setting, you step out of daily demands and give space for clarity and presence.
about.description2: Once a month, we gather in a small group (around 10 participants) for an evening designed to support everyone – whether you are leading others, studying, between jobs, or simply seeking balance in everyday life. The practice creates conditions for reflection, renewed perspective, and clarity.

expectations.title: What to Expect

items.description: ceremonial cacao prepared with homemade oat milk or water, a touch of salt, and honey. This natural drink supports focus, balance, and calm energy.
short, practical breathing and awareness exercises, guiding you through all five senses to bring presence and clarity.
live sounds and instruments to encourage relaxation and a fresh perspective.
optional, a brief round to share experience from the practice.

expectations.experience: No previous meditation experience is required.
expectations.language: The sessions are held in Norwegian, but you are welcome to respond in English, Latvian, or Russian.

about.title: Sound & Breath
about.subheading: A guided sound journey back to yourself
about.description1: is a gentle sound bath experience created to help you pause, breathe, and reconnect with yourself.
bodyParagraphs: In everyday life, we often carry stress, thoughts, responsibilities, and tension in the body. This session invites you to slow down and enter a peaceful space where you can simply rest and receive.

We begin with a guided body relaxation meditation, helping you soften each part of the body and arrive into stillness. After this, you are invited to lie down comfortably and experience calming sounds from Tibetan singing bowls, Koshi bells, rainstick, and other soothing instruments.
The sounds create a relaxing atmosphere that supports deep rest, presence, and inner calm.
No previous experience with meditation or sound bath is needed. You are welcome exactly as you are.

expectations.title: What to expect
bullets: Time to rest, breathe, and reconnect
A peaceful moment just for yourself

whoIsItFor.title: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Sound & Breath is for you who feel tired, stressed, overstimulated, or simply wish to take a pause from everyday life.
It is also for you who want to create more space for calm, clarity, and balance.

practicalInfo.title: Practical information
practicalInfo.bringValue: Comfortable clothes, warm socks, water bottle, and anything that helps you feel cozy

Inguna skaper en trygg atmosfære og har en egen evne til å holde energien i rommet slik at tankene faller til ro. Hver gang er opplevelsen litt annerledes, men jeg sitter alltid igjen med den samme følelsen: ‘Dette var nøyaktig det jeg trengte.’
items.name: Participant

items.message: Because of my profession and daily habits, my mind is usually running non-stop whenever I’m awake. When I join a mindfulness practice, the atmosphere helps me relax and quiet my thoughts almost instantly. I settle into a calm state of being present, here and now. Along the way, I often experience meaningful visions and insights that support me both personally and professionally. The practice gives my mind the restorative pause it needs to return to full speed afterwards.
items.name: Girts

items.message:
I would strongly recommend joining and discovering what it’s all about. No matter what stage of life you’re in, where you come from, or what your current state of mind is, we can all benefit from a moment of reflection and a deep breath. Here, you have the opportunity to experience exactly that.
Inguna is deeply passionate about her work. She creates a space of safety and invites you on an inner adventure without judgment or rush. What you gain from the circle is entirely up to you: maybe you simply need rest and reassurance, maybe you want to look at stresses in your life from a new perspective, or maybe you just want to be around open-minded people. Who knows 🙂
And yes— the cacao is delicious and of exceptionally good quality!

about.title: Relax with NADA
about.subheading: A calming reset for a busy mind
about.description1: is a nonverbal 45-minute ear acupuncture session created to help you slow down, settle your thoughts, and give your body and mind a moment of rest.
bodyParagraphs: In everyday life, our minds can stay busy long after the day itself has slowed down. Stress, thoughts, responsibilities, difficulty switching off, and problems with sleep can make it hard to truly relax and recover. This session offers you a simple space to pause, settle, and reset.
Five small acupuncture needles are placed in specific points in each ear. After this, you can sit or lie comfortably, listen to calming background music, breathe naturally, and rest.
The simplicity of NADA is part of what makes the experience special. There is nothing you need to explain, achieve, or perform during the session.
No previous experience with acupuncture is needed.

expectations.title: What to expect
bullets: Five NADA acupuncture points in each ear using sterile, single-use needles
Around 45 minutes to sit or lie down and rest
No need to talk, explain, or perform
A simple moment to pause, settle, and reset

whoIsItFor.title: Who is it for?
whoIsItFor.intro: NADA may be suitable for you if you would like a moment to slow down and support relaxation, especially during periods with:
paragraphs: I became interested in NADA partly because I know myself how difficult it can be to switch off when the mind keeps going. That is why I was curious about such a simple method where you do not need to talk or actively do anything — you can just sit, listen to calming music and let the body settle.
NADA is a supportive practice and does not replace medical assessment or treatment when this is needed.

certification.title: Try NADA during my certification period
certification.intro: As part of my NADA certification process, I will be giving NADA sessions to 30 people and collecting practical experience and feedback along the way.
certification.priceIntro: During this certification period, the session price follows the guidelines from NADA Norge:
certification.feedback: After the session, I will also ask for a short feedback about how you experienced it and, if relevant, how you slept that night.

practicalInfo.bringValue: Comfortable clothes. You do not need to bring anything special.
practicalInfo.pleaseSignUp: Please book a session before coming.
practicalInfo.cancellation: If you can't attend, please cancel your booking or send an SMS at least 24 hours before:

precautions.title: Please be aware
precautions.intro: Before booking a NADA session, please let me know if you:
bullets: have a medical implant or another condition that may be relevant to acupuncture
have an infection, inflammation, wound, or other problem affecting the ears
are feeling unwell or have a fever
paragraphs: I use sterile, single-use acupuncture needles for every NADA session.

If you are a blood donor, please be aware that acupuncture can affect when you are allowed to donate blood. Norwegian blood-donation rules may require a waiting period of up to six months depending on who performed the acupuncture and the equipment used. Please check with your blood bank if regular blood donation is important to you.
If you are unsure whether NADA is suitable for you, please contact me before booking.

background.title: A little about NADA
paragraphs: NADA was originally developed in the 1970s at Lincoln Hospital in New York as a supportive method for people going through addiction treatment. Since then, the standardized five-point ear acupuncture protocol has become widely used internationally, including within addiction treatment, mental health services and other settings where stress, inner restlessness and emotional strain are present.

The World Health Organization (WHO) has also recognized acupuncture as one of the supportive methods that may be used during withdrawal treatment, for example to relieve symptoms such as restlessness and sleeplessness.
Today, NADA is also used more broadly as a simple, non-verbal way to support relaxation and help people slow down during periods of stress, racing thoughts, inner restlessness or difficulty sleeping.

sections.title: I have always liked an active life
paragraphs: I have always been someone who enjoys working, taking responsibility and having a lot going on. I still do.
I like challenges. I like finding solutions. I like being involved and feeling that I am moving things forward. My daytime work is an important part of who I am, and I genuinely enjoy it.
For a long time, I also believed that being strong meant being able to keep going. If something was difficult, I would simply work harder, find another solution and move forward.
And for a long time, that seemed to work.

sections.title: When everything became too much
paragraphs: At the end of 2020, I went through burnout.
It did not happen in one dramatic moment. Looking back, there had been signs along the way, but I had become very good at ignoring them.
I was tired, but I kept going. I was stressed, but I told myself it was temporary. There was always something that needed to be finished first.
Until eventually my body and mind simply said enough.

That period was difficult, but it also became an important turning point in my life. It made me realise how easy it is to lose contact with ourselves when we are constantly focused on everything we have to do.
I started asking myself questions I had never really stopped to ask before.
How am I actually doing? What does my body need? What does rest really mean? And how do we notice that we are getting close to our limit before we cross it?

sections.title: I wanted to understand why
paragraphs: When I started to feel better, I became very curious about what had actually happened to me.
I did not only want to recover. I wanted to understand why I had ended up there in the first place.
That curiosity was one of the reasons I started studying Basic Medicine at Tunsbergs Medical School.
I wanted to understand more about the body, stress, health and the connections between different systems. But in many ways, I was also trying to understand myself.
The more I learned, the more I became aware that wellbeing is not only about what happens when something is already wrong.
It is also about learning to notice the smaller signals much earlier.

sections.title: Trying, learning and discovering
paragraphs: My curiosity did not stop with theory.
Over the years, I have taken part in different courses, classes, retreats, ceremonies and sessions. I have explored mindfulness, breathing, sound, cacao and other practices.
Some experiences were powerful. Some were simply interesting. And some were not for me at all.
I tried things on myself first.
I wanted to understand how they actually felt, not only how they were described.

Little by little, I started collecting the things that genuinely helped me. Practices that made it easier to slow down. To breathe differently. To become more aware of what was happening inside me. To create a pause before simply continuing with the next thing.
And perhaps most importantly, I learned that these practices do not need to be complicated.
Sometimes a small pause can change much more than we expect.

sections.title: Finding what works for you
paragraphs: I do not believe there is one practice, one method or one answer that works for everyone.
We are all different, and the way we find calm, balance and space for ourselves can be different too.
Sometimes we need movement. Sometimes we need stillness. Sometimes it is breath, sound, touch, reflection or simply a moment where nothing is expected from us.
The important thing is to notice what helps you.

That is also how I look at the practices I share through SF Nature. NADA, sound, breathing, mindfulness and cacao are different experiences, and each of them offers a different way to pause, reconnect and explore what feels right for you.
You may connect strongly with one of them, with several, or discover something completely different along the way.
For me, the goal is not to tell you which path to choose, but to create a space where you can try, notice and find what supports you best.
And perhaps, the better we become at noticing ourselves, the easier it becomes to recognise when we need that pause — before everything becomes too much.

sections.title: How SF Nature came to life
paragraphs: SF Nature grew slowly and naturally from this journey.
It was never about creating one particular method or telling people how they should live.
For me, it is simply a space where I can share some of the things I have learned, experienced and found helpful along the way.
Today, that includes NADA, sound, breathing, mindfulness and cacao.
Different practices, but with something in common: they all create a possibility to pause for a while.
I still love an active life. I still love my work, challenges and having things going on.
But now I understand much better that balance does not necessarily mean doing less.
Sometimes it means learning how to create small moments where we can stop, notice ourselves and reset before continuing.

sections.title: Why I want to share it
paragraphs: I know what it feels like to realise too late that you have been pushing yourself too far.
And I also know how much it can mean to discover small tools that help you come back to yourself.
That is what I would like to share through SF Nature.
Not promises. Not perfect solutions.
Just experiences, practices and small possibilities that may help someone notice themselves a little more, relax a little deeper, or perhaps find something that works for them.

lines: To you who are reading this…
I hope you remember to make space for yourself too.
Not only when everything becomes too much, but also in the middle of ordinary, busy life.
